outcome_statement: On every counted deal in the window, the node's own records show it came through on the terms it accepted: it paid as agreed when it bought, and when it provided, it recorded settlement for what it served and reported serving the model it named. Every record is checked against the signer keys the reader trusts; a deal with a record that does not check out is shown as unavailable, never as met or not met.
resolution_rule: a deal is resolved only when every term that applies to it is met
counterparty_note: The peer's book of the same exchange is not held on this node. It is shown as not_available, never as a failure or as agreement.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Paid as agreed
clauses.claim: When the node bought, every invoice it saw has a settlement its own wallet reported, for the invoice's amount. Every record is verified under the reader's trusted keys first: a deal with a record whose signature does not verify, or whose signer is not among those keys, is not_evaluable, and the two reasons are told apart.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Settlement recorded for what it served
clauses.claim: When the node provided, its records show the exchange it accepted terms for, and every invoice it issued has a settlement its wallet reported, for the invoice's amount. The pack proves what was recorded and settled; it does not prove the answer was good or that the provider's own report of what it ran is true. Records are verified under the reader's trusted keys, as for the term above.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Model it reported matches the model it named (its own report)
clauses.claim: When the node provided, the model it reports having run is the model it named. A deal a referee already adjudicated is not judged again: the row carries the sealed verdict, read for this node as the node's own verdict counts read it (corroborated, or contradicted naming the other half, is met; contradicted naming this node is not_met; anything else is not_evaluable). Otherwise the row reads "provider states": the node's own records of the model requested and the model that answered, which no verifier can check against the accepted terms, since those carry the model only inside their digest.
